    All Packages

    Package Summary
    Package
    Description
    org.iasi.base
    Defines application-independent return-code bits and visibility levels; it depends only on the JDK.
    org.iasi.common.i18n
    Loads localized catalogs without imposing console or logging presentation rules.
    org.iasi.common.logging
    Provides reusable logging ports, event sanitization and console/file adapters without application-context dependencies.
    org.iasi.common.operation
    Represents operation data and explicit status masks without deciding whether the caller continues execution.
    org.iasi.common.platform
    Identifies host operating-system, runtime and effective privilege information without performing machine provisioning operations.
    org.iasi.common.process
    Provides reusable process coordination primitives without application messaging, resource extraction or process termination policies.
    org.iasi.common.validation
    Converts textual values and checks reusable numeric and filesystem constraints without CLI or application dependencies.
    org.iasi.setupdev
    Contains the executable entry point for the development-ecosystem setup application.
    org.iasi.setupdev.args
    Loads CLI syntax, declares supported arguments and reconciles textual configuration layers before context publication.
    org.iasi.setupdev.configuration
    Reads bundled and external TOML configuration as textual argument data without creating or starting virtual machines.
    org.iasi.setupdev.console
    Presents application help and the temporary context summary; help bypasses operational logging formatting.
    org.iasi.setupdev.core
    Coordinates initialization, owns the single-threaded execution context and publishes validated effective values.
    org.iasi.setupdev.messages
    Reports application-specific initialization diagnostics using reusable console infrastructure and the execution return code.
    org.iasi.setupdev.targets
    Discovers target directories while leaving regex selection and machine operations to other components.
